Just asking for a little advice from you guys

You might be making mistakes because you didn't take the time to play these things slower to iron them out smoothly before you brought them up to speed. That's the easiest way to keep messing up. All people over-estimate their abilities, even really talented people. The solution is practice. Play every day in a focused way. Have a routine. Warm ups, exercises for a few minutes, then play through songs you already know and like, then leave a good 20 minutes to learn or work on something new.

Play with a metronome. Start slowly. Increase tempo when you play it perfectly every time. If you have a section you always mess up on, don't waste practice time playing the whole song: Play that passage to perfection. Once it's done, then put it all together. Rinse and repeat.
So would that transition into improvements with my improv playing?

Absolutely. It will help you with accuracy, which is useful everywhere. Also, working accurately at what was once a difficult speed at a what was once a difficult set of movements will become rote. The bar will raise, making you a better player across the board. Of course, it's important that what you're practicing matches your goals as a player. The biggest factors will be your position and your power. On the flat power vs. frontal area (what the wind impacts on) is the biggest this. You can increase your power or decrease your frontal area.
